title: Global sections over a strictly henselian local scheme are the stalk at the closed point
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with closed point $s$, and let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point lying over $s$ [def-weil-geometric-point] ($\Omega$ any algebraically closed field with a map $\kappa\to\Omega$). For every abelian sheaf $F$ on $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] the germ map $F(S)\to F_{\bar s}$, $a\mapsto a_{\bar s}$, sending a global section to its class at the pointed etale neighbourhood $(S,\bar s)$ in the stalk of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], is an isomorphism of abelian groups, natural in $F$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03QO (lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian), the statement Gamma(S,F) = F_sbar and its proof: for a pointed etale neighbourhood (U,ubar) of sbar and an affine open Spec A of U containing the image u of ubar, R -> A is etale and kappa(u) = kappa(s) (kappa(u) is finite separable over the separably closed kappa(s)); by Theorem Tag 04GG (theorem-henselian in etale-cohomology.tex, condition (8)/(10)) A = R x A' compatibly with the maps to the residue field, giving a section S -> U through ubar; hence (S,sbar) is cofinal (initial among neighbourhoods, as an index of the colimit) and the germ map is bijective. The proof works verbatim for any algebraically closed Omega over kappa, since the section sends sbar to ubar (both lie over u and induce the same map kappa(u)=kappa(s) -> Omega). DAG nodes for the section: lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting (i)=>(ii) and lem-weil-pbc-root-lifting-etale-retraction.

proof.text: *The germ map and its naturality.* Write $\mathcal N=\mathcal N_{\bar s}$ for the category of pointed etale neighbourhoods of $\bar s$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods]: objects $(U,\bar u)$ with $f_U:U\to S$ etale and $f_U\circ\bar u=\bar s$, morphisms $h:(U',\bar u')\to(U,\bar u)$ the $S$-morphisms $h:U'\to U$ with $h\circ\bar u'=\bar u$. By [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] $F_{\bar s}=\varinjlim_{(U,\bar u)\in\mathcal N^{\mathrm{op}}}F(U)$ in abelian groups (the diagram $D_F$ sends $(U,\bar u)$ to $F(U)$ and $h$ to the restriction $h^*:F(U)\to F(U')$), with coprojections $\iota_{(U,\bar u)}:F(U)\to F_{\bar s}$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Since $\mathrm{id}_S$ is etale and $\mathrm{id}_S\circ\bar s=\bar s$, $(S,\bar s)$ is an object of $\mathcal N$, and the germ map is $\gamma_F=\iota_{(S,\bar s)}:F(S)\to F_{\bar s}$, a homomorphism of abelian groups. For a morphism $\varphi:F\to G$ of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] the stalk map $\varphi_{\bar s}:F_{\bar s}\to G_{\bar s}$ is the canonical map induced by the compatible family $\iota^G_{(U,\bar u)}\circ\varphi_U$ (compatible because $\varphi$ commutes with restrictions), so $\varphi_{\bar s}\circ\iota^F_{(U,\bar u)}=\iota^G_{(U,\bar u)}\circ\varphi_U$ for every $(U,\bar u)$, in particular $\varphi_{\bar s}\circ\gamma_F=\gamma_G\circ\varphi_S$: the germ maps are natural in $F$. It remains to show that $\gamma_F$ is bijective (steps 2-7).

*An affine chart through the point.* Let $(U,\bar u)$ be an object of $\mathcal N$, $f=f_U:U\to S$, and let $u\in U$ be the image of the point of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ under $\bar u$. Since $f\circ\bar u=\bar s$ and $\bar s$ lies over $s$, $f(u)=s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhood-affine-shrink] (with $V=U$, $W=U$, $\bar v=\bar u$) there are a ring $A$, an open immersion $j:\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$ with $u\in j(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ and $f\circ j$ etale, and $\bar u_0:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $j\circ\bar u_0=\bar u$. Let $\mathfrak q\subset A$ be the prime with $j(\mathfrak q)=u$ (the image of $\bar u_0$). By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] the morphism $f\circ j:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R=S$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\phi$ for exactly one ring map $\phi:R\to A$; so $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and since $\operatorname{Spec}\phi$ sends $\mathfrak q$ to $\phi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ and $(f\circ j)(\mathfrak q)=f(u)=s$, which is the point $\mathfrak m$, we get $\phi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak m$: $\mathfrak q$ lies over $\mathfrak m$.

*The residue field does not grow.* By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable] applied to $\phi:R\to A$ and $\mathfrak q$ (with $\phi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak m$, step 2), the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is a finite separable extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak m)=\kappa$ via the map $\bar\phi:\kappa\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ induced by $\phi$. Since $R$ is strictly henselian, $\kappa$ is separably closed [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], so by [lem-pc-sepclosed-finite-sep-trivial] $\bar\phi$ is an isomorphism. Translation to the schemes [def-weil-residue-field]: the residue field of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ at $\mathfrak q$ is $A_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak q}=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, that of $S$ at $s$ is $\kappa$, and the open immersion $j$ identifies the local ring of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ at $\mathfrak q$ with $\mathcal O_{U,u}$; under these identifications the residue field map $f^\sharp:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)$ induced by $f$ at $u$ is $\bar\phi$ (the residue map of $f\circ j=\operatorname{Spec}\phi$ at $\mathfrak q$, composed with the isomorphism given by $j$). Hence $f^\sharp:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)$ is an isomorphism.

*A retraction through $\mathfrak q$ (Stacks Theorem 04GG, used in 03QO as $A\cong R\times A'$ compatibly with the maps to the residue field).* $R$ is henselian (strictly henselian includes henselian, [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]: idempotents of finite $R$-algebras lift uniquely mod $\mathfrak m$), so by [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting], (i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii), simple roots in $\kappa$ of monic polynomials over $R$ lift to roots in $R$. With step 2 ($\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ etale, $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak m$) and step 3 ($\kappa\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ an isomorphism), [lem-weil-pbc-root-lifting-etale-retraction] gives an $R$-algebra homomorphism $\tau:A\to R$, i.e. $\tau\circ\phi=\mathrm{id}_R$, with $\tau^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak q$.

proof.text: *The section.* Put $\sigma=j\circ\operatorname{Spec}\tau:S=\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$. By functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $f\circ\sigma=(f\circ j)\circ\operatorname{Spec}\tau=\operatorname{Spec}\phi\circ\operatorname{Spec}\tau=\operatorname{Spec}(\tau\circ\phi)=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{id}_R)=\mathrm{id}_S$, so $\sigma$ is a section of $f$, in particular an $S$-morphism from $(S\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}S)$ to $(U\xrightarrow fS)$. And $\operatorname{Spec}\tau$ sends the closed point $\mathfrak m$ to $\tau^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak q$, so $\sigma(s)=j(\mathfrak q)=u$.

*The section respects the geometric points: $\sigma\circ\bar s=\bar u$.* By [def-weil-geometric-point] a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ is the same as a point $x\in U$ together with a field homomorphism $\kappa(x)\to\Omega$; and the field map of a composite $g\circ\bar y$ is (field map of $\bar y$)$\circ$(residue map of $g$ at the image point) [def-weil-residue-field] (residue maps compose contravariantly, being induced by the local homomorphisms of stalks). Let $\alpha:\kappa(s)\to\Omega$ be the field map of $\bar s$ and $\beta:\kappa(u)\to\Omega$ that of $\bar u$; let $f^\sharp:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)$ be the residue map of $f$ at $u$ (an isomorphism, step 3) and $\sigma^\sharp:\kappa(u)\to\kappa(s)$ the residue map of $\sigma$ at $s$ (defined since $\sigma(s)=u$, step 5). (a) $f\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}_S$ gives $\sigma^\sharp\circ f^\sharp=\mathrm{id}_{\kappa(s)}$, hence $\sigma^\sharp=(f^\sharp)^{-1}$. (b) $f\circ\bar u=\bar s$ gives $\beta\circ f^\sharp=\alpha$. Now $\sigma\circ\bar s$ lies over $\sigma(s)=u$, as $\bar u$ does, and its field map is $\alpha\circ\sigma^\sharp=\beta\circ f^\sharp\circ(f^\sharp)^{-1}=\beta$, the field map of $\bar u$. Hence $\sigma\circ\bar s=\bar u$, and $\sigma$ is a morphism $(S,\bar s)\to(U,\bar u)$ in $\mathcal N$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods]. (Stacks takes $\Omega$ a separable closure of $\kappa$; the argument holds for every algebraically closed $\Omega$ over $\kappa$.)

*Cofinality: the germ map is an isomorphism.* By [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered] $\mathcal N$ is cofiltered. Let $\mathcal J\subset\mathcal N$ be the full subcategory on the single object $(S,\bar s)$; its only endomorphism is $\mathrm{id}_S$, since an $S$-morphism $h:S\to S$ satisfies $h=\mathrm{id}_S\circ h=\mathrm{id}_S$. By steps 2-6 every object $(U,\bar u)$ of $\mathcal N$ receives a morphism from $(S,\bar s)\in\mathcal J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory] (1) (with $\mathcal C$ the category of abelian groups, $\mathcal I=\mathcal N$, $D=D_F$) the canonical map $c:\varinjlim_{\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}}D_F|_{\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}}\to\varinjlim_{\mathcal N^{\mathrm{op}}}D_F=F_{\bar s}$, induced by the coprojection $\iota_{(S,\bar s)}$, is an isomorphism. The category $\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}$ has one object and one morphism, so it is connected and $D_F|_{\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}}$ is the constant diagram with value $F(S)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram] $(F(S),\mathrm{id}_{F(S)})$ is a colimit of it, and with this choice $c=c\circ\mathrm{id}_{F(S)}=\iota_{(S,\bar s)}=\gamma_F$. Hence the germ map $\gamma_F:F(S)\to F_{\bar s}$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups, natural in $F$ by step 1. (Explicitly: every germ $\iota_{(U,\bar u)}(x)$ equals $\gamma_F(\sigma^*x)$ for the section $\sigma$ of step 6; and if $\gamma_F(a)=0$ then, the colimit being cofiltered, $h^*a=0$ for some $h:(U',\bar u')\to(S,\bar s)$, and with a section $\sigma':(S,\bar s)\to(U',\bar u')$ one gets $a=(h\circ\sigma')^*a=\sigma'^*h^*a=0$, since $h\circ\sigma'$ is an $S$-endomorphism of $S$, i.e. the identity.)
